extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO disciplinary staff, and legal counsel involved in USPTO practitioner discipline
extracted.subtask_description: A final disciplinary order setting forth stipulated facts, legal conclusion, and agreed sanctions against a USPTO-registered patent practitioner, including applicable regulatory citations and required procedural actions during suspension and for reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO jurisdiction for disciplinary proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over this matter pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.19 and 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes the statutory and regulatory basis for initiating and resolving disciplinary actions against registered practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicable professional conduct rules by date
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility, 37 C.F.R. § 10.20 et seq., applies to practitioners' conduct occurring prior to May 3, 2013, while the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct, 37 C.F.R. § 11.101 et seq., apply to practitioners' conduct occurring after May 2, 2013.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine which set of rules governs alleged misconduct by reference to the date(s) of the conduct; here, Respondent's alleged misconduct occurred prior to May 3, 2013, so 37 C.F.R. § 10.20 et seq. applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proscription of disreputable or gross misconduct (37 C.F.R. §10.23(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent acknowledges that, based on the information contained in the stipulated facts, his conduct violated 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(a) (proscribing engaging in disreputable or gross misconduct).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulation is the substantive basis for discipline when practitioner conduct is disreputable or grossly improper; supporting facts (e.g., criminal conviction) are used to establish the violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim suspension authority (37 C.F.R. §11.25)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director commenced a proceeding under 37 C.F.R. § 11.25 seeking the interim suspension of Respondent, and the USPTO entered a Final Order suspending Respondent on an interim basis pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.25.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interim suspension may be sought and imposed under §11.25 where circumstances warrant; the order records the procedural invocation of that authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension length and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall be ... suspended from practice before the Office in patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters for twenty-four (24) months commencing on December 20, 2013.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sanctions specify both duration and scope (all practice before the Office, including patent, trademark, and non-patent matters).

rubrics_metrics.name: Right and procedure to seek reinstatement (37 C.F.R. §11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall be permitted to seek reinstatement pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 upon completion of the 24-month suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinstatement is not automatic; it must be sought under §11.60 and is subject to regulatory conditions and review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent compliance with 37 C.F.R. §11.58
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order imposes §11.58 compliance as an affirmative obligation on the suspended practitioner (the regulation's specific procedural/content requirements apply).

rubrics_metrics.name: OED Director compliance with 37 C.F.R. §11.59
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office must follow §11.59's procedures (as applicable) in connection with publication, notice, and other post-discipline obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation not to apply for or obtain a USPTO customer number during suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not apply for or obtain a USPTO customer number unless and until the Office grants a petition under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 reinstating Respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspended practitioners are barred from obtaining a customer number (i.e., cannot resume platform access) until formal reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request removal from power of attorney documents and customer numbers (within 30 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 30 days of the date of this Final Order, Respondent shall (1) request in writing that he be removed from all power of attorney documents and USPTO customer numbers on which Respondent reasonably believes his name appears and (2) make such request of all persons that Respondent reasonably believes have the authority to remove his name from such power of attorney documents and USPTO customer numbers, such as Respondent's current employer, Respondent's former employer(s), Respondent's current client(s), and Respondent's former client(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The practitioner must proactively request removal from records and inform relevant parties (employers, former employers, current/former clients) within a specified short timeframe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit of compliance and documentary proof (within 45 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 45 days of the date of this Final Order, Respondent shall provide the OED Director with (1) an affidavit attesting to his compliance with the provisions of the prior subparagraph and (2) copies of the written request(s) sent in compliance with the provisions of the prior subparagraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof of compliance is required and must be submitted to the OED Director within the specified timeframe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic publication of Final Order (OED FOIA Reading Room)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish this Final Order at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's electronic FOIA Reading Room, which is publicly accessible at http://e-foia.uspto.gov/Foia/OEDReadingRoom.jsp.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final disciplinary orders are published publicly via the OED FOIA Reading Room to provide transparency and public notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Official Gazette notice consistent with provided text
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish a notice in the Official Gazette that is materially consistent with the following: [Notice of Suspension text describing Respondent, registration number, suspension for violating 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(a), factual basis, and reference to OED Reading Room].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office issues an Official Gazette notice summarizing the discipline; the order provides the materially consistent text to be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of disciplinary record in future proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Agreement or this Final Order shall prevent the Office from considering the record of this disciplinary proceeding (1) when addressing any further complaint or evidence of the same or similar misconduct concerning Respondent brought to the attention of the Office; (2) in any future disciplinary proceeding against Respondent (a) as an aggravating factor to be taken into consideration in determining any discipline to be imposed and/or (b) to rebut any statement or representation by or on Respondent's behalf; and/or (3) in connection with any request for reinstatement submitted by Respondent pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The disciplinary record may be used offensively or defensively by the Office in later matters and may function as an aggravating factor or rebuttal evidence in future proceedings, including reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED Director to file motion to dismiss pending proceeding (14 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall file a motion to dismiss the pending disciplinary proceeding with the administrative law judge within fourteen (14) days of the date of this Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a settlement agreement resolves charges, the Office will move to dismiss related pending administrative proceedings within the prescribed short timeframe.
